component_records.title: Program design, curriculum and credential architecture
component_records.description: Delivers the industry-informed online AI curriculum for Track A and Track B, built with an employer advisory group that reviews technical skills and learning milestones each cohort. The curriculum is structured as an immersive schedule that can run part-time or full-time, with defined skill-attainment assessments at each milestone and a stated credential (or explicit statement that none is issued) on completion. Curriculum development is completed or finalised in the mobilisation phase and refreshed each cohort against employer input, and the design documents the monthly timeline through first-cohort placement, training duration, cohort size and stipend level.

component_records.title: Outreach, recruitment and application/assessment process
component_records.description: Runs a targeted recruitment campaign for New Yorkers underrepresented in tech who cannot reasonably access training on their own, with channel plans for CUNY/SUNY campuses, community-based organisations and workforce partners. Delivers an online application and evaluation process with a documented low-income eligibility determination, a needs assessment that records each participant's barriers to success, and an individual success plan that routes supports accordingly. Recruitment targets are set to meet or exceed the 250-participant floor with a stretch plan above 400, and to keep low-income enrolment above 50%.

component_records.title: Training delivery, stipends and wrap-around supports
component_records.description: Delivers and manages the cohort-based training itself: instruction, cohort management, attendance and progress tracking, and professional development support throughout training. Each participant receives a stated stipend at the proposed level plus wrap-around supports — a mentor and a career coach with industry expertise, plus barrier-specific supports identified in the needs assessment. Delivery is staffed for both part-time and full-time schedules so participants with employment or caregiving obligations can complete the program.

component_records.title: Employer partnerships and placement engine
component_records.description: Cultivates and maintains relationships with leading New York tech employers to inform curriculum content and generate paid internship and full-time AI openings, supported by employer commitment letters submitted with the proposal. Runs a placement function that matches participants to paid internships (Track A) and full-time AI roles (Track B), prepares them for interviews, and tracks placements through to hire. Placement support is designed to meet the commitment that the majority of graduates secure paid internships or full-time employment in AI or a closely related field.

component_records.title: Performance data, reporting and ESD access
component_records.description: Implements a participant data system that captures every required data point — applicant, enrolment and completion counts with low-income percentages, paid internship and full-time placement rates with low-income percentages, participating colleges and employer partners — and makes the data available to ESD on request. Produces the progress reports and periodic meeting cadence that support ESD's performance assessment, and reports against the three annual performance metrics (participants served, low-income completion rate, placement rate) estimated in the proposal. The data model is built to absorb the additional data points ESD fixes during contract negotiation without re-platforming.

component_records.title: Budget, pricing and cost justification
component_records.description: Delivers a line-by-line budget per track, mapped to the 18-month program duration and capped at $2M per track, with personnel services broken out by job title, named staff, rate, fringe and percentage of time, and OTPS costs on separate lines. Budget lines cover staff salary and benefits, wraparound supports and the participant stipend level, and other program costs including curriculum development, marketing and events. Indirect costs are excluded entirely, and any cost match the bidder offers is indicated in the budget template to earn the additional scoring points.

component_records.title: Compliance, diversity and contract obligations
component_records.description: A dedicated compliance workstream carries the non-technical obligations of the contract: MWBE participation at the 30% goal and SDVOB participation at the 6% goal, with OCSD-4 Utilization Plans, good faith effort documentation, quarterly Workforce Utilization Reports and monthly SDVOB compliance reporting; insurance placement at the required limits with ESD named additional insured and waiver of subrogation; lobbying-law and ethics compliance including the restricted-period contact rules and periodic 139-j/139-k updates; vendor responsibility registration and ongoing responsibility; and acceptance of Schedule A, OSC approval and change-order procedures.
